lessons.title: Take the if branch
lessons.description: Finish `evaluate_grade`. Conditional statements execute code blocks based on conditions. Use `if` and `else` to return "Pass" if grade >= 50, otherwise "Fail". The test checks that `evaluate_grade(80)` equals `"Pass"`; `evaluate_grade(40)` equals `"Fail"`.
learning_objectives: The if branch runs only when its comparison succeeds, and else runs otherwise.

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 4.1. if Statements — Conditional Control

exercises.question: The if branch runs only when its comparison succeeds, and else runs otherwise.
hints: A failed comparison skips the first branch.
Eight meets a cutoff of five, so the first branch runs.
score = 8 / if score >= 5: /     print('pass')
exercises.explanation: The if branch runs only when its comparison succeeds, and else runs otherwise.

exercises.question: A score of eight meets a cutoff of five. Which word comes from the first branch?
hints: The comparison succeeds.
The first branch says pass.
pass
exercises.explanation: Eight is at least five, so pass runs.

exercises.question: Eight points against a cutoff of five. Which word is displayed?
hints: The cutoff is met.
The word shown is pass.
pass
exercises.explanation: The if branch prints pass.

exercises.question: Build the one-line branch that prints pass when score is at least five.
hints: Start with if and the score name.
Then the cutoff and the print.
if score >= 5: print('pass')
exercises.explanation: if score >= 5: print('pass') is the branch.

exercises.question: Fill the comparison that treats five as good enough for the first branch.
hints: The score should meet the cutoff.
Greater-or-equal belongs in the blank.
exercises.explanation: >= treats five itself as good enough.

exercises.question: A score sitting exactly on the cutoff took the fallback. Which line makes the cutoff exclusive?
hints: The stored score is the cutoff itself.
The header uses a strict greater-than.
Line 2
exercises.explanation: Line 2 excludes the cutoff, so five takes the else.

exercises.question: Thirty degrees against a freeze point of thirty-two. Which word is displayed?
hints: The temperature is below the freeze point.
The fallback word is thaw.
thaw
exercises.explanation: 30 is below 32, so thaw is printed.

exercises.question: Print high when the number meets ten, otherwise low.
hints: The blank should treat ten itself as high.
Greater-or-equal ten returns high.
exercises.explanation: label(10) prints high.

lessons.title: Check the next branch
lessons.description: When you have more than two branches, use `elif`. Implement `temperature_status(temp)` returning "Cold" (< 15), "Warm" (15..28), or "Hot" (> 28). The test checks that `temperature_status(10)` equals `"Cold"`; `temperature_status(20)` equals `"Warm"`; `temperature_status(35)` equals `"Hot"`.
learning_objectives: elif tries another comparison only after every earlier branch was skipped.

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 4.1. if Statements — Conditional Control

exercises.question: elif tries another comparison only after every earlier branch was skipped.
hints: A second if would run even when the first branch already did.
Seventy-five misses one hundred and meets seventy, so warn runs.
heat = 75 / if heat >= 100: /     print('stop') / elif heat >= 70: /     print('warn')
exercises.explanation: elif tries another comparison only after every earlier branch was skipped.

exercises.question: Kiln heat is seventy-five. Which word is chosen when one hundred is the first cutoff and seventy is the next?
hints: The first cutoff fails, so the next one is tried.
The next branch says warn.
warn
exercises.explanation: 75 misses 100 and meets 70, so warn runs.

exercises.question: A kiln sits at seventy-five. What status word is displayed?
hints: One hundred is too high a bar for this reading.
The displayed word is warn.
warn
exercises.explanation: The elif branch prints warn.

exercises.question: Build the opening branch that prints stop once heat reaches one hundred.
hints: Start with if and the heat name.
The cutoff is one hundred, then the print.
if heat >= 100: print('stop')
exercises.explanation: if heat >= 100: print('stop') is the first branch.

exercises.question: Fill the keyword that tries the seventy cutoff after the first branch is skipped.
hints: It introduces the next comparison, not the fallback.
The keyword is elif.
elif
exercises.explanation: elif checks seventy only when one hundred failed.

exercises.question: A blazing kiln printed two status words. Which line should have been the follow-up branch?
hints: The opening branch is the right first check.
The later header is another if, so both can run.
Line 4
exercises.explanation: Line 4 is a second if, so 110 prints both stop and warn.

exercises.question: A cold kiln sits at forty. Which status word is displayed?
hints: Neither cutoff is reached.
The fallback word is calm.
calm
exercises.explanation: 40 misses both cutoffs, so calm is printed.

exercises.question: Return warn for a reading of seventy-five, using a follow-up branch.
hints: The blank is the follow-up keyword.
Seventy-five should return warn.
elif heat >= 70:
exercises.explanation: status(75) prints warn.
exercises.starter_code:
def status(heat):
    if heat >= 100:
        return 'stop'
    ___ heat >= 70:
        return 'warn'
    return 'calm'
print(status(75))

lessons.title: Practice Meltdown Mitigation
lessons.description: Control a nuclear reactor with multi-condition if/elif/else logic. 1. is_criticality_balanced(temperature, neutrons_emitted): return True when the reactor is balanced, i.e. temperature is below 800 AND neutrons_emitted is above 500. 2. reactor_efficiency(voltage, current, theoretical_max_power): compute the percentage (voltage * current / theoretical_max_power) * 100 and return its band: green for >= 80, orange for >= 60, red for >= 30, and black below 30. 3. fail_safe(temperature, neutrons_produced_per_second, threshold): compare temperature * neutrons_produced_per_second with the threshold and return LOW below 90% of the threshold, NORMAL from 90% up to and including 110%, and DANGER above 110%. The test checks that is_criticality_balanced(750, 600) equals True; is_criticality_balanced(800, 600) equals False; reactor_efficiency(200, 50, 10000) equals 'green'.
